newsitem.title: USA: Oil explosion on US Gulf Coast causes minor spill.
newsitem.headline: Oil explosion on US Gulf Coast causes minor spill.

text.p: An explosion on an oil platform caused a minor spill and injured four workers Tuesday afternoon in Barataria Bay near New Orleans, Louisiana, U.S. Coast Guard officials said.

"The spill was a minor one, and it may not even have to be cleaned up. The only trace of the spill so far is the sheen on top of the water," said Commander Kenneth Parris of the U.S. Coast Guard in New Orleans, Louisiana.
Parris said none of the injuries were life threatening and two of the workers would probably be released from the hospital Wednesday morning.
Parris said the platform, owned by Samson Resources Co, was small and out of service and was comprised of oil producing equipment on top of an old barge.
The barge had a storage capacity of 3,000 barrels. It had been out of service for several years and was being refurbished by workers of Triple G Construction when the explosion occurred.
"They were testing on a daily basis for explosive gases, and someone was working on something which caused a spark which caused an explosion," said Parris.
Parris said the explosion would be investigated by the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration.
